did_you_know.text: Did you know? Absalom created a royal image for himself: a chariot, horses, and fifty men running ahead of him.

Did you know? Absalom used his encounters with people seeking justice at the city gate to claim that no one had been appointed by the king to hear them, even though he himself had not been appointed a judge.
Did you know? Scripture summarizes Absalom’s actions in these words: “So Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel”—that is, he gradually won their support through his conduct.
Did you know? Absalom organized his rebellion through messengers sent throughout all the tribes of Israel, instructing them to proclaim him king in Hebron when they heard the sound of the trumpet.
Did you know? Two hundred men from Jerusalem went with Absalom in good faith, and Scripture emphasizes that they knew nothing about the rebellion’s plan.
Did you know? Ahithophel, who had been David’s adviser, joined Absalom. As a result, the rebellion gained strength, and the number of Absalom’s supporters increased.
Did you know? Among the loyal men who left with David were the Kerethites, the Pelethites, and six hundred Gittites—warriors from Gath who had joined him and marched before him.
Did you know? Ittai the Gittite declared his complete loyalty to David: he swore to remain with the king in both life and death.

Did you know? David refused to take the Ark of God with him in his flight and ordered it returned to Jerusalem, saying that if he found favor in the LORD’s eyes, he would return and see it and His dwelling place again.

Did you know? When David heard that Ahithophel had joined the rebels, he prayed, “LORD, please turn Ahithophel’s counsel into foolishness.” He then sent Hushai the Archite to Jerusalem to frustrate Ahithophel’s advice.
